about: verbatim pre-registered rule texts the experiment rules quote (copied 23 Oct 2026 from RULES_20261101.json, written 22 Oct 02:30 PKT and later dated additions, and /tmp/claude-0/sci2/RULES.md, written 22 Oct 15:48 PKT); never edited

RULES_20261101.written: 2026-10-22 02:30 PKT, before any candidate result in this prep was computed

held_out_designs.temperature: national OOF design (0.5-degree spatial cells -> 5 folds x alternate 14-day blocks, national_train.py): a correction for fold k is fitted only on rows of the other folds; the locked test cells (station-lake/archive/national/test_locked.json, 48 points) are never used to fit anything and are scored separately
held_out_designs.height: leave-band-out: fit the residual model on stations at or below a cut (3,500 m and, separately, 4,000 m), score the stations above the cut; the envelope acts only on rows above the training maximum of that fit
held_out_designs.landslide: time split as in landslide_basis_fit.py: fit 2022-01-01..2024-12-31, test 2025-01-01 onward; per-tehsil bootstrap (1000)
held_out_designs.forward_1nov: on 1 Nov the same designs are re-run on the data to 31 Oct, plus a forward test of every temperature candidate on 2026-10-01..2026-10-31 (fit only on data to 2026-09-30)

RULES_20261101.uncertainty: temperature: two-way cluster bootstrap, B = 1000, stations and calendar days resampled together (McCullagh 2000). Landslide: tehsil bootstrap B = 1000. Intervals are 95 % percentile intervals

rules.A_zone_daypart_season_offset: PROMOTE if, for the target stratum (plains night hours 20-05 PKT, and separately hills all hours), the 95 % lower bound of (current MAE - candidate MAE) > 0 (Holm-adjusted across the two targets), AND in every zone the lower bound > -margin, AND on the locked test points the lower bound > -margin
rules.B_offset_by_forecast_temperature_bin: same as A; B replaces A only if B also beats A with lower bound > 0 in the target strata; otherwise the simpler passing candidate is kept
rules.C_range90_mondrian: PROMOTE if under the candidate every zone x day-part cell with >= 300 held-out hours has 90 % coverage within [0.87, 0.93], the current served ranges fail this in at least one cell, and the 95 % lower bound of (current interval score - candidate interval score) > -0.03 x current interval score (Gneiting and Raftery 2007, alpha = 0.10)
rules.H_height_envelope: PROMOTE only if, on rows whose station height exceeds the fit's training maximum, the 95 % lower bound of (MAE full residual - MAE faded residual) > 0 at BOTH cuts (3,500 m and 4,000 m). Otherwise the current behaviour stays. A positive result at one cut only is reported as inconclusive (not promoted)
rules.L_landslide_basis_map: PROMOTE the mapping only if, held out 2025-01-01 onward and scored with the INSTALLED odds model (landslide-odds-91.17.283-monotone, features P1 and P3), the 95 % interval of the improvement (raw - mapped) is above zero for the KS distance of P1 and of P3 AND for the mean |log OR error| on days the training basis rates Low or above (OR >= 2). P7 is no longer a model feature and is reported only. Primary candidate (named 22 Oct 02:50 PKT, before running it): L1 = the same empirical quantile mapping fitted per rain-climate group (province x height class) for EVERY tehsil (no per-tehsil knots: 3 years of one tehsil cannot fix its 99th percentile), P1 and P3 only. L0 (the 21 Oct per-tehsil method) is re-scored with the installed model for diagnosis only
rules.S_coast_seabreeze: same form as A for the coast zone (target stratum: coast, all hours), with the onshore-wind term; must also not be worse at Karachi stations' heatwave hours (lower bound > -margin)
rules.reporting_only: as-issued day-0 archive score, air-quality issued score and the Hapdija / Mandi Kushlak check are reported, never promoted by themselves
rules.H2_height_fade_to_top_band: ADDED 22 Oct 03:05 PKT after H was inconclusive (full residual above the ceiling: bias +1.6/+2.0 C; H faded to zero: bias -1.9/-2.0 C) and BEFORE H2 was computed: above the training ceiling the tree residual fades over Lz = 600 m not to zero but to the mean residual measured at the training stations in the top 500 m below the ceiling, by PKT 3-hour block. Same test and rule as H: promote only if the 95 % lower bound of (MAE full - MAE H2) > 0 at BOTH cuts; it must pass again in the 1 Nov run. Note: tested on the same held-out rows that showed H inconclusive (forking-paths risk), hence the repeat requirement
rules.BLENDR_blend_weights_rebalanced: ADDED 22 Oct 2026 ~09:40 PKT, before any BLEND-R result. Candidate: refit the Step-2 multi-model blend start (station-lake/scripts/step2_blend.py: convex weights, no intercept, per zone x lead x 3-h block) with (V1) per-network row weights so urban MACH rows carry the same total weight as all other networks together in every fit cell, or (V2) MACH rows dropped. Current = V0 (unweighted, as served). Held-out design: leave-station-out, 0.5-degree cells -> 5 folds (crc32-balanced as national_train.py); weights for a fold never see its stations; locked points and non-representative stations never fitted. Truth: national table obs, with the PMD AWS hours overlaid from the newest LAMHA hourly file (incl. 1 Sep - 31 Oct 2026), scored on the blend START (no chain), leads 1, 2, 3, 5 pooled. Score: hourly MAE; two-way cluster bootstrap stations x days, B = 1000. PROMOTE a variant only if (i) overall gain (V0 MAE - Vk MAE) has its lower bound > 0 at the 97.5 % one-sided level per variant (Bonferroni over the two variants: 1.25th percentile > 0), AND (ii) in every zone and in the urban MACH stratum the 1.25th percentile > -max(0.05, 0.03 x V0 MAE). If both pass, the one with the larger lower bound. Reported, not part of the rule: rural PMD AWS daily Tmin (00-08 PKT) bias and bulletin Tmin. Serving: the blend start is not switched by a data file in the current build; a pass is written as 'passed - weights file ready, needs the Step-2 serving hook'
rules.NONREP_stations: ADDED 22 Oct 2026 ~09:40 PKT. nonrepresentative_stations.json lists stations whose 2 m reading does not represent the area served (first entry: aws:Kandia_Warisabad Thooty Bar_ARG_1, 1,362 m rain-gauge site on a 39.5 deg SW slope, persistent held-out bias -2.6 C). They are dropped from national training (locked_filter.py) and scored only as their own stratum. The national refit without them is judged by the paired rule (national_paired.py): champion = current recipe on its own window WITH them; challenger = refit to 31 Oct WITHOUT them; both scored on the same held-out rows, which exclude them || AMENDED 24 Oct 2026 08:29 PKT by owner decision (v91.17.283.14), before the 1 Nov run: no station list is used. nonrepresentative_stations.json is kept as history only and read by no script. Every observed value goes through NIGRAAN's value-level quality control (server/api/obsqc.mjs via scripts/lib/obsqc_truth.py, run step obs_qc): failing values are never fitted and never scored; the station's other values stay. national_paired.py now judges champion = current recipe (every value) against challenger = refit without the failing values, on the same held-out rows (passing values only). A station whose values are judged wrong all the time loses them automatically (Kandia_Warisabad Thooty Bar_ARG_1: its temperature and humidity are marked in data/obs-qc-marks.json under the verification-not-worse rule of the v91.17.283.14 replay).

RULES_20261101.conditioning: extreme-day strata (hot-season heat, winter cold) are selected on the FORECAST (raw T0 daily max >= its zone-season 90th percentile; raw T0 daily min <= its zone-season 10th percentile), not on the observation, to avoid the forecaster's dilemma (Lerch et al. 2017, Statistical Science 32: 106)

SCI2.R1:
## R1 · A3 flood hourly-rain trigger on 2022 (re-test of RULES.md item 3; method unchanged)
Rain: IMERG V07 half-hourly, D:\NIGRAAN\inputs\IMERG_subhourly_PAK\IMERG_subhourly_PAK_2022{06..09}.nc, season 15 Jun - 30 Sep 2022,
the SAME script a3_imerg_season.py (year made a parameter, nothing else changed): max clock-hour rain, max PKT-day total, days >= 25 mm.
Truth: the 2022 composite Flood_2022.shp (the only 2022 outline in hand; no dated 2022 outline exists in the cloud or the laptop
folders: TU Wien 2022 and UNOSAT 3342 not copied). Frame = bounding box of its polygons (as fx_grid). Same tehsil rule as 2025:
centroid in frame, >= 40 non-riverine cells; non-riverine = > 29 km from the major-river centre-lines (the domain fixed in
fx-model.json / item 3; not re-chosen). Event = tehsil non-riverine flooded share > frame-wide share. Predictors P_hour, P_ladder
(served flood.rainBands 2.3/5.3/7.2/7.7 mm/h rung 0..4), P_day, P_d25. AUC and Spearman, 95 % bootstrap over tehsils (2000, seed 3).
Decision (two years):
  - the served ladder is "supported" in a year only if its AUC CI lies above 0.5 (P_ladder reported as served; P_hour as its driver);
  - a sourced replacement (P_day, the WS5 day-total trigger; P_d25, days >= 25 mm, the event the calibrated rain chance predicts) is
    PROMOTED only if in BOTH 2025 and 2022: its AUC CI lies above 0.5 AND its paired AUC difference vs P_hour has a CI above 0.
  - pooled 2025+2022 (tehsil-year bootstrap stratified by year) is reported only, never decides.
Otherwise NOT PROMOTED: nothing served changes.
SCI2.R2:
## R2 · Flood extent forecast (fx_rp, RULES.md item 8 candidate) against dated truth
Models (no refit on any test data): C3 = JRC depth at the reach-event's return period >= d AND 30 m HAND <= h; B2 = JRC wet at the
1-in-10 map (the comparator). Parameters: for 2024 and 2025 events, d = 14 dm, h = 20 m and B2 RP = 10 as fitted in fx_rp_test.json
on 2010/2014/2022. For the 2022 composite (a training event of that fit) both C3 (d, h) and B2 RP are REFITTED on 2010 + 2014 only by
the same procedures (C3 grid max pooled CSI; B2 area matching) so 2022 is held out (LOEO).
Domain, reach zones, representativeness rule, HAND band, JRC tiles and the Gumbel event return period: exactly fx_rp_test.py.
Flow for a dated window [d0, d1]: the GloFAS reanalysis season-to-date peak at the reach gauge cell, 1 Jul .. d1 of that year (water on
the floodplain at d1 reflects the largest flow so far; no lag parameter is chosen). 2022 composite: season peak 1 Jul - 15 Oct (as before).
Truth layers (flood only, normal water excluded where the product separates it):
  2024 (UNOSAT 3971, VIIRS 375 m): the 8 windows' MaximumFloodExtent (the "_1" duplicate of 17-20 Aug used only if it differs; the
       first file otherwise); observed = AnalysisExtent (the product's single analysis extent, 21 Jul - 3 Aug file, used for every
       window unless a window carries its own) minus that window's CloudObstruction. MinimumFloodExtent is reported only.
  2025 (UNOSAT 4197): HJ-2B 16 Aug FloodExtent within its AnalysisExtent; S2 20 Aug FloodExtent (no analysis layer: observed = the
       convex hull of its Flood+Water polygons, reported as such); S1 27-28 Aug FloodExtent_Punjab within AnalysisExtent_Punjab; VIIRS
       26 Aug - 7 Sep FloodWaterExtent within AnalysisExtent minus CloudObstruction (this layer includes normal water: the JRC map also
       marks river channels wet; noted, both models are scored on the same cells).
  2022: Flood_2022.shp, observed = its frame (as fx_calibrate).
Cells: 250 m grid cell centre rule (as fx_grid). A reach-window zone is scored if it has >= 200 observed cells and >= 50 % of the
zone's domain cells observed (fx_calibrate's admission rule with "observed" for "in frame").
Scores: CSI per window (areas summed over its zones); per-window gain = CSI(C3) - CSI(B2).
Pooled statistic: G = mean over the 3 years (2022, 2024, 2025) of the year gain, year gain = mean of that year's window gains
(each year weighs equally; the 8 correlated VIIRS windows do not dominate). 95 % CI: bootstrap of reach zones, resampled within each
year independently (a resampled reach carries all its windows of that year), 2000 draws, seed 2026.
PROMOTE (fx-model served) only if the lower bound of G's CI > 0 AND no year's gain point estimate is < 0. Otherwise NOT PROMOTED.
Reported only: per-window CSI/POD/FAR/area bias, year CIs, the Min-extent variant for 2024, the 2025 composite (already seen).
Extension (not waited for): TU Wien 2022 (GFM, dated S1) and UNOSAT 3342 (dated 2022) would replace the 2022 composite by dated 2022
windows with their own observed masks; 2022 then enters G as the mean of its windows, parameters still LOEO (2010+2014).
SCI2.R2_addendum:
## R2 addendum (written 22 Oct 2026 ~17:05 PKT, before any 2022-dated or 4163 layer was loaded; rule, statistic, CI and parameters unchanged)
The coordinator's instruction: the dated 2022 windows REPLACE the 2022 composite; 4163 is added to 2025. Copies verified complete
against HISAAB sizes (3342 208,366,571 B and 4163 116,350,633 B = receipt archive_bytes; TU Wien FLOOD-HM-MASKED.zip 364,339,308 B =
publisher record size). Windows, each with its own observed mask, read in place from the zips (no unzip):
  UNOSAT 3342 (2022): S1 06 Aug Sindh, S1 15 Aug Sindh Province, S1 27 Aug Sindh+Balochistan: FloodExtent within AnalysisExtent;
                      VIIRS 03-23 Aug: FloodExtent within AnalysisExtent minus CloudObstruction.
  TU Wien (Roth et al. 2022, doi 10.48436/zvvmh-nan78, 20 m Sentinel-1, values 0 dry / 1 flood / 255 masked): one window per UTC
                      acquisition day (14 days, 10 Aug - 23 Sep): truth = any frame of that day flags flood at the 20 m pixel holding
                      the 250 m cell centre (the same centre rule as every other layer); observed = any frame of that day valid there.
  UNOSAT 4163 (2025): S2 31 Jul 2025 FloodExtent within AnalysisExtent minus CloudObstruction.
Flow: season-to-date peak 1 Jul .. window date (as R2). Parameters: 2022 windows use the 2010+2014 LOEO refit (d 13 dm, h 20 m, B2 RP 10,
already computed); 2024/2025 the fixed ones. Zone admission as R2. 2022 year gain = mean of its scored windows (TU Wien and UNOSAT
windows equally weighted, as all windows within a year). Promote iff pooled G CI lower bound > 0 and no year gain < 0. The composite
2022 is reported only.
